excluded: Training and held-out deck variants as strategy authorities
Raw private guide text at runtime

informationPolicy.normalEvaluation: The acting player may use its own private state and all public history. Opponent hidden cards, exact remaining order, prizes and private choices are unavailable.
informationPolicy.opponentBeliefs: Public cards, public actions, legal deck-construction relationships and prior matchup knowledge may update confidence-weighted hypotheses. An inference never becomes an observed fact.
informationPolicy.benchmarkIsolation: A benchmark may schedule an exact opponent list, but the specialist receives only the information allowed by normalEvaluation unless the result is explicitly labelled hindsight.

evidenceClasses.meaning: Directly visible in the current information state or public history.
A supported possibility with an explicit confidence and public evidence trail.
A material possibility that remains open and must be represented in search or trigger abstention.

prohibited: Reading the real opponent hand, deck order or prizes
Using later reveals to grade an earlier fair-information decision
Treating a scheduled deck ID as player-visible knowledge
Treating a guide matchup percentage as an outcome label

strategicConcepts.definition: A concrete route to end the game, including primary, alternate and denial routes plus the public triggers that justify switching between them.
The minimum credible sequence of knockouts for each player, adjusted for prize values, bench liabilities, multi-prize turns and denied attacks.
Who can execute a meaningful attack or denial turn first and how attachments, evolution, retreat, item lock and disruption change that schedule.
Pressure that advances a credible prize or board-control route rather than damage without a follow-up.
Actions that deny the opponent's next credible prize route through durability, healing, protection, mobility, board restraint or hand and energy disruption.
Preservation and expenditure of finite cards, Energy, recovery and deck count according to the chosen win condition.
Ordering draw, search and chance actions so later commitments use the most public and private information legally available to the acting player.
A justified change between primary and alternate win conditions when public commitments or resource depletion change which route is credible.

tiers.meaning: Best-supported action set for the current beliefs and strategic plan.
A sound alternative whose expected strategic result is not materially worse.
A modest strategic loss that preserves the principal win condition.
A substantial loss of tempo, prize position or win-condition progress.
An action that foreseeably abandons or concedes the principal credible win condition.

abstainOn: Unsupported or unaudited card interaction can change the ranking
A material opponent hypothesis is missing from the search
Search coverage is too shallow to distinguish the top tiers
Guide and learned evaluator materially disagree without reviewed evidence
A later hidden reveal would be required to justify the label
confidencePolicy.rule: Low or insufficient confidence produces assumptions and open questions, not a mistake grade.

correctionsAndPromotion.strategicCorrections: A human correction creates a versioned playbook edit and a weighted reviewed scenario. It is not an outcome label or unconditional move rule.
correctionsAndPromotion.candidatePolicy: Self-play and training produce a versioned candidate specialist and never overwrite the active specialist.

source.title: The Ultimate Crustle Guide
source.usage: Paraphrased strategic evidence only. Earlier guide sections may describe cards absent from the frozen list.

identity.primaryPlan: Use Mega Kangaskhan ex to buy setup time while constructing one highly resilient Crustle, then deny the opponent enough effective answers to complete the prize race.
alternatePlans: Pivot into Mega Kangaskhan ex pressure after the opponent commits resources to answering Crustle.
Win a resource or deck-out contest when taking prizes would improve the opponent's response and the public clocks favor Crustle.
failureConditions: The only viable Crustle is exposed before its required protection and Energy functions are established.
Unnecessary bench liabilities give the opponent a cheaper prize or trap route.
The specialist takes a prize that activates disruption before it can survive the response.

principles.statement: Prefer going first and use an available Mega Kangaskhan ex as the early active while developing the minimum board needed for the selected Crustle route.
triggers: opening choice is available
Mega Kangaskhan ex is an opening option
avoid: Benching extra liabilities without a matchup reason
Treating the early Kangaskhan prize value as automatically fatal

principles.statement: Default to one fully protected Crustle against Dragapult because an unnecessary second Crustle can become a gust, item-lock and movable-damage target. Add a second only when the first cannot remain the winning route, the trap resources are publicly exhausted, or both Crustle can be protected and a specific Handheld Fan or late-game route justifies the exposure.
triggers: The first Crustle is lost or cannot be kept alive
The represented trap route is publicly exhausted
Both Crustle can receive relevant protection and the second has a named role
avoid: Adding a second Crustle merely because bench space is available
Exposing an underprotected Crustle to Budew, Risky Ruins, Dudunsparce and Munkidori loops

principles.statement: Value each special Energy by the attack, effect or damage threshold it answers; attachment count alone is not a sufficient readiness measure.
triggers: multiple Energy types are available
the opponent represents effect-based or return-damage counterplay
avoid: Spending the only relevant protection on a nonessential target
Assuming all attached Energy are interchangeable

principles.statement: Delay a nonterminal first knockout when one more setup turn materially improves survival against the opponent's represented disruption; take the knockout when delay loses the board or ends the game less reliably.
triggers: taking a prize enables hand disruption
one additional attachment or heal changes the response threshold
avoid: Passing without comparing both players' clocks
Taking a prize solely because damage is available

principles.statement: Use gust and hand disruption to remove or exhaust the small set of public attacker and recovery classes that can answer the selected fortress plan.
triggers: an answer is publicly committed
the opponent cannot rebuild the answer in one turn
avoid: Spending Boss's Orders on a target that does not advance the active win condition
Claiming a hidden answer is present without evidence

principles.statement: When the opponent commits its limited Energy, attacks or protection answers to Crustle, compare the cost of continuing with the cost of transitioning to a prepared Mega Kangaskhan ex.
triggers: opponent resources are committed to Crustle
Mega Kangaskhan ex can become ready before the next required attack
avoid: A surprise pivot without sufficient attachments
Committing Hero's Cape before the attacker choice is settled

principles.statement: Against Dragapult, attach Handheld Fan to the Active Mega Kangaskhan ex early when attack damage, a movable Energy and an opposing Bench target make the Tool live. Each successful trigger increases attachment debt while Crustle develops; if Dragapult declines to attack, Kangaskhan can become a pressure attacker and Boss's Orders can target Drakloak.
triggers: Mega Kangaskhan ex is Active and expected to take attack damage
The attacking Pokemon is expected to retain movable Energy after the attack
The opponent has a legal Benched Energy destination
avoid: Assuming damage counters trigger Handheld Fan
Treating the Tool as disruption when no legal Energy move exists

principles.statement: Use Eri when the revealed hand contains Items whose removal changes the next response. Taking the first knockout and playing Eri on the same turn is an alternative to delaying the prize when it can remove Unfair Stamp or another critical response before it becomes usable.
triggers: The opponent's likely Item response determines whether Crustle survives
A first knockout would activate a comeback Item
avoid: Treating Eri as mandatory without valuable revealed Items
Encoding an outdated three-copy count

principles.statement: After the opponent takes Mega Kangaskhan ex and reaches three or fewer Prize cards, evaluate Special Red Card as an immediate hand-reset option. Prefer it only when reducing the current hand is more valuable than preserving the Item for a later disruption turn.
triggers: The opponent has three or fewer Prize cards remaining
Mega Kangaskhan ex was just removed and the opponent has accumulated a strong hand
avoid: Calling Special Red Card legal before its Prize condition is met
Playing it automatically into a weak or already disrupted hand

principles.statement: When Budew blocks Item-based setup and no Dwebble is in play, Lumiose City can find Dwebble. Complete the turn's Supporter and attachment first, then use Lumiose last because its search ends the turn. If Hilda is the Supporter, take Crustle and an Energy, attach before Lumiose, and evolve the searched Dwebble on a later turn. Replacing Risky Ruins with Lumiose also means the searched Dwebble enters without Risky Ruins damage.
triggers: Budew item lock is active
The board lacks Dwebble
Ending the current turn does not concede the game
avoid: Using Lumiose City without accounting for its turn-ending cost
Assuming Hilda and evolution occur on the same ended turn

sourceClaims.claim: Lumiose City is the non-Item Dwebble route under Budew, and missing Dwebble is the central failure mode in that matchup family.
Lumiose City's search ends the turn.
Hilda can take Crustle and an Energy before Lumiose is used.
The searched Dwebble evolves on a later turn.
Lumiose replaces Risky Ruins, so Risky Ruins does not damage the searched Dwebble.
Risky Ruins damages newly played Basic Pokemon while it is in play.

principles.statement: For the frozen Crustle list, keep three attached Energy on the Active Crustle when Jumbo Ice Cream is part of the survival plan. Every Energy card in this frozen list provides one Energy, so the card and provided-Energy counts coincide here.
triggers: The Active Crustle is damaged
Jumbo Ice Cream is available or a required future out
Energy removal can reduce the attachment count below three
avoid: Assuming an attack-ready Crustle is also heal-ready
unresolved: For multi-Energy cards, whether 'Energy attached' counts Energy provided or attached Energy cards remains open pending the governing ruling.

sourceClaims.claim: Jumbo Ice Cream heals only a damaged Active Pokemon with at least three Energy attached.
The guide's survival plan protects the three-Energy healing threshold.
The multi-Energy interpretation is unresolved and is not generalized from the frozen list.

principles.statement: Against Hammer Dragapult, prioritize Mist Energy and Spiky Energy roles before additional Growing Grass Energy. The guide's resilient target is two Mist plus two Spiky when the game allows it, forcing multiple successful Hammer removals across distinct protection jobs.
triggers: The opponent represents Crushing Hammer, Phantom Dive, Mind Bend or a non-ex attacker
Multiple special Energy choices are available
avoid: Treating the four-Energy target as mandatory when tempo requires an earlier attack
Treating Energy types as interchangeable

principles.statement: When Handheld Fan moves Energy, concentrate it on one opposing Benched Pokemon when possible. Later, use Boss's Orders to bring that Pokemon Active and knock it out so the accumulated Energy is discarded. This is especially valuable when Dragapult opens with Budew.
triggers: Handheld Fan moves an Energy from an attacker
A legal opposing Bench destination exists
avoid: Scattering moved Energy without a matchup reason
Assuming damage counters trigger Handheld Fan

sourceClaims.claim: Stack Fan-moved Energy on one Benched Pokemon and later gust and knock it out to discard the stack.
Handheld Fan is particularly useful when Dragapult develops through Budew.
The player who owns Handheld Fan chooses the Energy destination.

matchups.plan: Develop one protected Crustle behind an Active Mega Kangaskhan ex. Use Handheld Fan, Eri, Special Red Card and functional Energy attachments to stretch Dragapult's attack chain without exposing an unnecessary second Crustle.
matchups.secondCrustleRule: Default no. Add one only when the first route fails, the trap resources are publicly exhausted, or both can be protected and the second has a named Fan, backup or late-game role.

matchups.plan: If both players open Mega Kangaskhan ex, evolve one Crustle but do not spend attachments charging it; preserve it for the long deck-out game. If only this player opens Kangaskhan, early aggression can force the opponent to dig and spend resources when the board supports it. Otherwise, develop one large Crustle for the long war.
matchups.technicalNote: Lillie's Determination shuffles its player's hand into the deck, then draws eight cards at exactly six Prize cards remaining and six otherwise. If the post-play hand plus deck contains no more than that draw amount, resolution empties the deck and, unless the game ends or the deck is replenished, that player loses on the next required draw. Xerosic's Machinations does not make Lillie's illegal; it can make this threshold easier to reach.

sourceClaims.claim: The mirror uses different development when both players open Kangaskhan, only this player opens Kangaskhan, or neither does.
Lillie's Determination shuffles the hand into the deck and then draws eight at exactly six Prizes remaining, otherwise six.
A combined post-play hand and deck no larger than the draw amount leaves the deck empty after resolution.
A player required to draw from that empty deck loses unless another event intervenes first.
Xerosic reduces a larger opposing hand to three but does not prohibit Lillie's Determination.

versionConflicts.detail: Earlier guide advice references Crushing Hammer, Psyduck, Cornerstone Ogerpon ex, Bianca's Devotion and Hand Trimmer, none of which appears in the frozen v1 manifest.
versionConflicts.resolution: Do not create executable card-specific instructions for absent cards. Preserve their transferable strategic concepts until a different list is explicitly versioned.
versionConflicts.reviewNote: The user confirmed that these guide sections are outdated but their underlying strategic ideas remain applicable.

source.title: How to Play Crushing Hammer Dragapult
source.usage: Paraphrased strategic evidence only. Later updates take precedence when they describe the frozen list.

identity.primaryPlan: Develop a sustainable chain of Dragapult ex attacks, use damage placement to construct the shortest credible prize route, and combine Energy denial with hand disruption to make the opponent miss a response.
alternatePlans: Use Budew when item lock costs the opponent more tempo than the retreat and attachment cost paid by Dragapult.
Use non-ex attackers, Munkidori and targeted disruption when an opposing protection plan makes direct Dragapult attacks inefficient.
Delay a knockout to deny a draw trigger or prepare a multi-prize turn.
failureConditions: The specialist initiates without enough Energy or evolved backup attackers to sustain the exchange.
Damage placement creates useful counters for the opponent without a concrete knockout route.
An unnecessary bench liability gives up the intended prize map or consumes required attachments.

principles.statement: Sequence broad draw, selective draw and search according to which action reveals information and which specific outs must remain searchable.
triggers: multiple draw or search effects are available
a known out or deck-bottom fact changes the preferred order
avoid: Searching a specific card before exhausting a higher-value information action without reason
Using hidden future information to justify the sequence

principles.statement: Plan attachments across the active, backup Dragapult and Munkidori so the deck can attack on schedule after a knockout or Crushing Hammer result.
triggers: an attachment choice is available
the active attacker is likely to be removed
avoid: Spending an attachment on a low-impact retreat when it breaks the next Phantom Dive
Developing one attacker without a recovery route

principles.statement: Use Budew when the expected item denial and survival window outweigh the retreat, attachment and delayed-attack cost; benching it for a later free promotion may be stronger than retreating immediately.
triggers: the opponent materially depends on items
Budew can survive or force a costly answer
avoid: Automatic item lock into an immediate knockout
Losing the next Phantom Dive solely to reach Budew

principles.statement: Initiate the Dragapult exchange when the attack takes meaningful prizes or forces the opponent in before it is ready and when backup attackers can sustain the resulting prize race.
triggers: a Phantom Dive is available
both boards are developing toward an exchange
avoid: Being first to attack a fully developed board without a follow-up
Taking a low-value prize that improves the opponent's response

principles.statement: Place damage counters according to a named future knockout or denial route and account for whether the opponent can move, heal or exploit that damage first.
triggers: Phantom Dive or Adrena-Brain damage can be allocated
a multi-prize route is reachable
avoid: Leaving convenient damage for the opposing Munkidori
Damaging a potential trap target before the trap line is resolved

principles.statement: Prefer disruption packages that jointly create a missed attack: Energy denial, hand reduction, gust pressure and item lock should be evaluated by the turn they buy rather than their isolated card value.
triggers: the opponent has a narrow response
Crushing Hammer or hand disruption can remove a required component
avoid: Using Crushing Hammer on an attachment the opponent can abandon cheaply
Spending Unfair Stamp without a concrete response denial

principles.statement: Against Crustle, normally wait until a Crustle has a second attached Energy before using Crushing Hammer so abandoning that attacker is costly. Use Hammer earlier when removing the only Mist immediately enables attack counters or confusion, removing Spiky protects a planned non-ex attack, or reducing the Active below three attached Energy cards disables Jumbo Ice Cream.
triggers: A Crustle has committed a second Energy
The only Mist or Spiky Energy blocks the immediate planned line
One removal denies the three-card Jumbo Ice Cream threshold
avoid: Removing the first generic Energy when Crustle can cheaply abandon the target
Treating all special Energy as equivalent

principles.statement: When Crustle opens Mega Kangaskhan ex, reach Phantom Dive before the protected Crustle is complete. On the second Phantom Dive that knocks out Kangaskhan, Judge can punish the large hand accumulated through Run Errand.
triggers: Mega Kangaskhan ex is the opponent's early Active
The opponent has accumulated a large public or inferred hand
The second Phantom Dive can take the knockout
avoid: Playing Judge without comparing it to the current hand and other supporter options
Racing with only one attacker and no credible follow-up

principles.statement: Place Phantom Dive counters on a benched Crustle that lacks Mist while taking Mega Kangaskhan ex, or use Boss's Orders to expose a different underprotected Crustle. If Dwebble used Ascension on turn one, pressure the evolved Crustle immediately with Mind Bend or Drakloak rather than allowing protection to accumulate.
triggers: A benched Crustle lacks Mist Energy
A turn-one Ascension publicly identifies the developing fortress
The active target and residual counters advance one coherent route
avoid: Placing counters that do not advance a named knockout route
Ignoring a more immediate route to prevent the fortress from stabilizing

principles.statement: Dudunsparce is a non-ex attack route into Crustle, but avoid attacking into active Spiky Energy. Remove Spiky with Crushing Hammer or use Boss's Orders to bring up a Crustle that does not have Spiky. If Boss's Orders instead brings Dudunsparce Active, Run Away Draw can return it and its attachments to the deck before another Active is promoted when the Ability is usable.
triggers: The direct Dragapult route is inefficient into Crustle protection
Spiky Energy is absent or can be removed or bypassed
Dudunsparce can attack without breaking the subsequent Energy plan
avoid: Attacking into active Spiky retaliation
Using Dudunsparce when the Energy commitment breaks the next required attack

sourceClaims.claim: Avoid attacking into Spiky Energy; remove it with Crushing Hammer or gust a Crustle without Spiky.
Run Away Draw returns Dudunsparce and its attachments to the deck when usable.
A new Active is promoted after the Active Dudunsparce leaves play.
Land Crash into Spiky places two counters on Dudunsparce, allowing Superb Scissors for 120 to knock out its remaining 120 HP; without Spiky it has 20 HP left.

matchups.plan: Use the approved v1.1 race, disruption and protection-aware attack plan. Handheld Fan on an Active Kangaskhan remains an unresolved attack-planning gap because each qualifying damaging attack can move one of the attacker's Energy to its own Bench.
unresolved: The guide gives no supported plan for repeatedly attacking an Active Kangaskhan holding Handheld Fan.

sourceClaims.claim: A qualifying attack that damages the Active Handheld Fan holder must move one Energy from the attacker to a legal attacker-side Bench destination when both exist and the Tool remains active.
The Dragapult guide's Crustle section does not supply a plan for this Handheld Fan attack loop.

openingPreference.reason: The cited preference was written for an older one-Budew, two-Night-Stretcher count; the frozen list has two Budew and three Night Stretcher.

matchups.plan: Use the guide's mirror sequencing, attachment and initiation principles, but apply the go-second preference only after the opponent archetype is public. A blind game-one choice follows the shared go-first policy.
unresolved: The revised two-Budew, three-Night-Stretcher list may change the magnitude of the guide's go-second preference.

versionConflicts.detail: The guide contains chronological updates. The frozen list matches the post-Worlds section with two Budew, three Ultra Ball, three Night Stretcher, Judge, four Psychic and two Darkness Energy.
versionConflicts.resolution: Use later list-specific advice when older card-count assumptions conflict, while retaining compatible general principles.
